    Campus Facilities
Moran College Central Library

        The library of Moran College
houses a total collection of 34,458
books and serves as a vital academic re-
source for both students and faculty
members. It subscribes to 3 magazines
and 6 daily newspapers, ensuring access
to current information and diverse read-
ing materials. The library provides a
seating capacity of 100 users, offering a
comfortable and conducive environ-
ment for study and research.

        In addition to its physical re-
sources, the library offers access to over
30,000 e-journals through the One Na-
tion One Subscription (ONOS) initia-
tive, significantly enhancing research
opportunities. Users can also download
more than 1,000 PDF books for aca-
demic purposes.

         The library is fully automated
using Koha, an open-source library
management software, which stream-
lines its operations. Furthermore, users
can conveniently search and access the
library’s collection through the Online
Public Access Catalogue (OPAC),
making information retrieval efficient
and user-friendly.
 Campus Facilities

 Auditorium
 The auditorium of Moran College is a
 spacious and well-equipped venue with
 a seating capacity of around 1000 stu-
 dents. It features a large stage and
 serves as a central hub for hosting cul-
 tural programmes, seminars, meetings,
 and various academic and co-curricular
 activities throughout the year.
 Campus Facilities
 Laboratory facility

 Moran College has well equipped labora-
 tory facilities that support both practical
 learning and research across Arts and Sci-
 ence streams. In the Arts faculty, depart-
 ments such as Geography and Education
 are provided with dedicated laboratories.
 The Geography laboratory is furnished
 with maps, surveying instruments and other
 essential tools that enable students to gain
 hands-on experience in cartography and
 field-based studies. The Psychology labor-
 atory of the Department of Education is
 equipped with various testing materials and
 apparatus to help students understand psy-
 chological experiments and assessment
 techniques in a practical manner.

 In the Science stream, the college has fully
 functional laboratories for Physics, Chem-
 istry, Botany, and Zoology. These laborato-
 ries are designed to meet the academic re-
 quirements of undergraduate courses and
 are equipped with modern instruments,
 specimens, chemicals and experimental
 setups. Students are encouraged to carry
 out experiments, projects and practical
 work under the guidance of experienced
 faculty members.

 Additionally, the Department of Computer
 Science is supported by a well-maintained
 computer laboratory with adequate sys-
 tems.
 Campus Facilities
 Shilpa Kala Sangrahalaya

 Moran College houses a unique Shilpa
 Kala Sangrahalaya with a remarkable
 collection of 3011 rare evergreen gram-
 ophone records along with several
 gramophone record players. Maintained
 within the college library, the museum
 is accessible to students as well as visi-
 tors, offering them an opportunity to ex-
 plore and appreciate vintage music and
 audio heritage. The museum also pre-
 serves a valuable collection of tradi-
 tional Assamese household articles, ag-
 ricultural tools, bamboo and cane crafts,
 indigenous musical instruments, and
 ethnographic materials reflecting the
 rich cultural heritage of Assam.
    Campus Facilities

Indoor Stadium
Moran College has a well-developed
Indoor Stadium, constructed with finan-
cial assistance from the University
Grants Commission (UGC). The facil-
ity is used for regular training and prac-
tice in indoor sports such as badminton
and table tennis. Provision is also made
for games like Arm wrestling, carrom,
with guidance from instructors and
part-time coaches to nurture students’
skills.
 Campus Facilities

 Swimming Pool
 Moran College has a well-maintained
 swimming pool measuring approxi-
 mately 50.00 m × 21.00 m × 1.80 m,
 providing facilities for both students
 and outsiders. The college also offers a
 certificate course in swimming, which
 is conducted regularly to promote phys-
 ical fitness and skill development.
 Qualified coordinators and supporting
 staff supervise the training and activi-
 ties, ensuring proper guidance and
 safety for participants.
 Campus Facilities

 Hostel Facilities
 The college provides separate hostel fa-
 cilities for both girls and boys, located
 within the campus. As seats are limited,
 accommodation is offered primarily on
 the basis of merit and the distance of the
 student’s residence from the college.
 Admission to the hostels is made
 through prescribed application forms
 submitted to the respective superinten-
 dents. The hostels are intended for dis-
 ciplined students, and their admission
 and conduct are strictly governed by the
 Moran College Hostel Rules, copies of
 which are available in the hostel office.
 Campus Facilities

 Outdoor Stadium                         &
 Playground
 Moran College has a spacious outdoor
 stadium and playground that serve as
 the main venue for various sports and
 athletic activities. The college has es-
 tablished a strong presence in sports un-
 der Dibrugarh University, particularly
 in outdoor events such as athletics,
 cricket, and football. The facilities sup-
 port regular practice, inter-college com-
 petitions, and tournaments, encourag-
 ing students to actively participate in
 sports and maintain physical fitness.
 Campus Facilities
 College Canteen
 Mississippi, the college canteen of Mo-
 ran College, serves as a convenient and
 welcoming space for both students and
 staff within the campus. The canteen
 provides a variety of hygienic and af-
 fordable food items, catering to the daily
 needs of the college community. It offers
 a comfortable environment for refresh-
 ment and informal interaction, thereby
 contributing to a vibrant campus life.
 With an emphasis on cleanliness, qual-
 ity, and accessibility, Mississippi plays
 an important role in supporting the well-
 being and convenience of students and
 staff throughout the academic day.
 Social Responsibility & Environmental Awareness

                                    NSS Unit, Moran College
                                    The National Service Scheme (NSS) Unit of Moran College plays a vital role in promoting
                                    community service, social responsibility, and personality development among students.
                                    Guided by the motto “Not Me But You,” the NSS Unit actively engages volunteers in various
                                    outreach and awareness programmes, including cleanliness drives, plantation campaigns,
                                    health and hygiene awareness programmes, blood donation camps, environmental conservation
                                    initiatives, and community development activities. The remarkable contribution and dedication
                                    of the NSS Unit have brought significant recognition to the institution, including the prestig-
                                    ious Best NSS Unit Award for the year 2022–23 conferred by Dibrugarh University. Further-
                                    more, Dr. Shrutaswinee Gogoi of Moran College received the Best NSS Programme Officer
                                    Award (Female) for 2022–23, while Mr. Sourav Deb was honoured with the Best NSS Vol-
                                    unteer Award (Male) for 2022–23 by Dibrugarh University. Through its continuous efforts,
                                    the NSS Unit of Moran College inspires students towards leadership, civic consciousness, and
                                    selfless service, thereby contributing positively to society and nation-building.




  Eco Club, Moran College
  The Eco Club of Moran College plays an active role in promoting environmental awareness
  and sustainable practices among students and the local community. It regularly organizes
  workshops, orientation programmes and popular talks to educate students on important
  environmental issues such as biodiversity conservation, climate change, waste manage-
  ment, and sustainable living. Through its interactive workshops, the Eco Club provides
  practical knowledge on topics like plantation drives, waste segregation and eco-friendly
  habits. Orientation programmes are conducted to sensitize students about environmental
  responsibilities and to encourage their active participation in green initiatives. Popular talks
  include experts, academicians and environmentalists, creating a platform for meaningful
  discussion and knowledge exchange.
 Social Responsibility & Environmental Awareness

 Cine Club, Moran College
 The Cine Club of the Department of English, Moran College, is a
 lively space where students come together to enjoy, discuss, and ap-
 preciate cinema beyond entertainment. Through film screenings and
 conversations, the club nurtures creativity, critical thinking, and a
 deeper understanding of stories, cultures, and human experiences.


 MEMBERSHIP IS OPEN TO ALL




                                            Orchidarium
                                            To promote biodiversity conservation and environmental sustaina-
                                            bility, Moran College has established an Orchidarium containing
                                            nearly 30 species of orchids generously donated by students of the
                                            college. The Orchidarium, developed as a joint initiative of the col-
                                            lege and the Department of Botany, serves as a living repository of
                                            orchid diversity and aims to create awareness among students re-
                                            garding the importance of plant conservation, ecological balance,
                                            and preservation of natural heritage.




 Vermicompost Unit
 Moran College has established a Vermicomposting Unit as
 part of its commitment towards environmental sustainability
 and eco-friendly campus practices. The unit promotes the
 scientific management of biodegradable waste through the
 use of earthworms for the production of organic compost.
 The unit also serves as a practical learning resource for stu-
 dents, encouraging environmental responsibility and green
 living within the campus community.

 Eligibility Criteria & Academic Framework of Four-Year Undergraduate Pro-
gramme (FYUGP) under NEP 2020
The Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of the
National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, offering flexibility, multidisciplinary learning, and multiple entry and
exit options. The programme is designed to provide holistic education with academic mobility and skill devel-
opment opportunities.

1. Minimum Eligibility Criteria for Admission
(i). Candidates seeking admission into the Four-Year Undergraduate Programme must have passed the Higher
Secondary (Class XII) Examination or equivalent from a recognized Board/Council.
(ii). Admission shall be conducted in accordance with:
      Guidelines issued by the Government of Assam
      Regulations of the affiliating University
      Norms prescribed under the SAMARTH Admission Portal

2. Multiple Entry and Exit Options of the Programme
In accordance with NEP 2020, the FYUGP provides flexibility for students to exit and re-enter the programme
at different stages. The structure is as follows:

a. First Year (After completion of 2 Semesters)
A student who successfully completes the first year of the programme shall be eligible for:
     Undergraduate Certificate
     The student may choose to exit the programme or continue to the second year.

b. Second Year (After completion of 4 Semesters)
A student who successfully completes two years of the programme shall be eligible for:
     Undergraduate Diploma
     The student may either exit with the diploma or continue to the third year.

c. Third Year (After completion of 6 Semesters)
A student who successfully completes three years of the programme shall be awarded:
     Bachelor’s Degree
     The student may either exit with the degree or continue to the fourth year for advanced specialization.

d. Fourth Year (After completion of 8 Semesters)
i. Bachelor’s Degree with Honours
A student completing the fourth year shall be awarded:
     Bachelor’s Degree with Honours
     This stage provides advanced disciplinary knowledge and specialization.

ii. Bachelor’s Degree with Honours and Research
A student who:
      Secures the required academic performance (as prescribed by the University), and
      Successfully completes a Research Project/Dissertation shall be awarded:
      Bachelor’s Degree with Honours and Research
3. Lateral Entry and Re-entry Provisions
     Students exiting the programme at any stage may be permitted to re-enter the programme within the
       stipulated period as per University rules.
     The re-entry shall be facilitated through the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) mechanism, enabling ac-
       cumulation and transfer of credits.

3. A student shall have to study the academic programme as per the scheme of the Programme. Even if a
candidate earns the required number of credits before completion of the full duration of the programme,
he/she shall not be entitled for the degree.

Course Enrolment
1. The minimum and maximum credits to be opted by a student for qualifying of a Undergraduate pro-
gramme shall be as per the Course Structure - Single Major and Double Major.
2. Change in Major: Students shall be allowed to change the Major at the end of the second semester. In
such a case the Minor will be converted as the Major so that the credit earned by the student remains the
same. In such case the earlier Major discipline in the 1st and 2nd semester will be treated as Minor disci-
pline. The HEIs may create 10% additional seats over and above the sanctioned strength to accommodate
the request for a change of major.
3. Change in Minor: Students shall be allowed to change Minor courses of his/her areas of interest within
the broad discipline at the end of the third semester. If a student pursuing a major obtains a minimum of 12
credits from another course then the student will be awarded Bachelor degree in previous with a minor in
later.

Attendance
1. The Course Teacher shall be responsible for maintaining a record of attendance of students who have
enrolled for the course.
2. All Course Teachers shall intimate the Principal through the Head of the Department concerned at least
thirty calendar days before the last instruction day in the semester, the particulars of all students who have
less than 75% of attendance during the total number of class days.
3. A student who has less than 75% attendance in average shall not be permitted to sit for the End semester
examination. However, that it shall be open to the University to grant exemption to a student who has
attended a minimum of 70% classes but failed to obtain the prescribed 75% attendance for valid reasons,
on recommendation of the Principals of the College on payment of a prescribed fee(s).
4. The Principals of the Colleges shall announce the names of all students who shall not be eligible to take
the End-semester examinations in the various Programmes and send a copy of the same to the Controller
of Examinations. Such candidates shall have to repeat the concerned Course(s) when it is offered next.
5. A student declared as dis-collegiate shall not be allowed to proceed to the next higher Semester. He/she
shall need to pursue the Semester afresh in which he/she was declared as dis-collegiate along with the next
fresh batch.

Provision of Multiple Exit:
Exit 1: There is a provision of exit after successful completion of 1 year (two semesters). A Certificate will
be awarded when a student exits at the end of year 1 (2 semesters). Students who have secured minimum
 of 40 credits will be awarded a UG certificate (in the field of study/discipline) if, in addition, they complete
one work based/skill based vocational course/internship of 4 credits within one year from the completion
of 2nd semester examination.
Exit 2: There is a provision of exit after successful completion of 2 years (four semesters. A Diploma will
be awarded when a student exits at the end of year 2 (4 semesters). Students who have secured minimum
of 80 credits will be awarded a UG Diploma (in the field of study/discipline) if, in addition, they complete
one work based/skill based vocational course/internship of 4 credits within one year from the completion
of 4th Semester examination.
Exit 3: Three Year UG Degree Programme (BA, B. Sc, B. Com and Bachelor in other discipline) with
single/double major: There is a provision of exit after successful completion of 3 years (six semesters).
Students who wish to undergo a 3-year UG programme shall be awarded UG degree in the major discipline
after successful completion of three years, securing 120 credits.
Four Year UG Programme with Honours (BA, B.Sc., B. Com and Bachelor in other discipline) with
single/double major: Students who wish to undergo a 4-year (8 semester) UG programme shall be awarded
UG Honours degree in the major discipline after successful completion of four years with Discipline Spe-
cific Elective Courses in 7th and 8th semesters in lieu of Research Project and Dissertation, securing a
minimum of 160 credits.
Four Year UG Programme with Honours with Research (BA, B.Sc., and Bachelor in other discipline)
with single/double major: Students who wish to undergo a 4-year (8 semester) UG programme shall be
awarded UG Honours with Research degree in the major discipline after successful completion of four
years, with Research Project and Dissertation in 7th and 8th Semesters, securing 160 credits.

institution and is officially registered under the Societies Act. Alumni members contribute sig-

donations of almirahs, books, microphones, and other essential resources. The association has
also contributed towards infrastructural development by funding facilities such as the badminton
court in the Indoor Stadium. Alumni actively participate in various cultural and social activities

of the activities are:
